# Index

39 pages in 10 sections; latest page update 2026-11-24.

## Start here

1. **Summary:** [Summary](00-overview/summary.md). From eleven phone photos and no tape, AI agents built a credible, parametric, articulated 3D model of a teleoperation rig, accepted by an independent reviewer and viewable in a browser; its sizes are unchecked photo estimates. Since 2026-11-24 a platform grows around it: step 1, agent control and live sharing between browsers, is live on mightwork.ai.
2. **Lessons learned:** [Lessons learned](60-lessons/lessons-learned.md). Fifty-five numbered lessons (L-01 to L-55) from building a 3D asset from photos with a team of AI agents, each one sentence with its evidence and how it is now applied, grouped by topic, with a top ten and a map to the failures and patterns behind them.
3. **Model card:** [Model card of the Rig B asset](70-results/rig-b-model-card.md). What the Rig B asset is, what it is for and what it must not be used for - 46 parts in five groups, 20 joints (6 of them assumed), 14 reference frames and 305 parameter records with their sources and ranges, built from eleven photos; sizes are photo estimates never checked against a tape, and all three of the owner's figures conflict with the photos.
4. **Next steps:** [Next steps](90-next/next-steps.md). What to do next, in priority order and by whom: platform step 1 is live (2026-11-24) and the owner tries it; then a tape session with four questions for the owner, a planted-error test of the reviewer, the Skill on a second object, small fixes, other rig configurations, the assessment and simulator phases, and routine maintenance.

D-01 to D-20 come from the approved plan, D-21 to D-37 from the first build, D-38 to D-46 from platform step 1 and D-47 to D-55 from agent interface v2 (all 2026-11-23 and 24). *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*

## Plan

- [The approved plan](30-plan/approved-plan.md): Version 3 of the plan, approved by the owner on 2026-11-23, rewritten for the wiki. It judged the task feasible as a structural, articulated, re-measurable layout model, with sizes and looks not yet shown, and set out a five-stage method built on parametric code, honest size ranges, scripted checks and an independent reviewer. *(stable, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Deviations from the approved plan](30-plan/deviations.md): What was done differently from the approved plan and why. The largest change is the owner's direction to run a full implementation autonomously, which replaced the plan's human gates, owner clicks and separate acceptance author with reviewer rounds and the coordinator's checks in the browser. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The platform plan (version 7)](30-plan/platform-plan.md): The second plan, approved by the owner on 2026-11-24, in plain words. It turns rigtwin from one model into a working platform in five steps that can each be stopped after - agent control, honest numbers, assessment, an agent in the app, a control room - with an independent simplicity monitor. Step 1 is built; what it changed from the plan is listed here. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*

## Method

- [The agent process](40-method/agent-process.md): How the agents were organised in this run - a coordinator, an infrastructure agent, a measurement agent, three modellers in parallel, an independent reviewer, two interface reviewers and an implementer - what each brief contained, how collisions were avoided, and which parts of the approved process were not exercised. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The asset contract](40-method/asset-contract.md): The specification an asset must satisfy - units and axes, naming, parameter records, the spec file, what a component module exports, materials, the GLB conventions, every field of the description file, the three kinds of variable, the shared pose definition and the budgets. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Checks](40-method/checks.md): Every automatic check of the asset and the platform (bun run check, 28 checks, 8 of them added by platform step 1 for the commands, the server, the live page and the deploy), of the distribution build (2) and of the viewer page (53), with what each verifies, the real failure it exists to catch, and its current result; plus the host's load test, what is not checked and how to add a check. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
- [Decomposition and connections](40-method/decomposition.md): How an object is split into components - one structural tree plus tags for function - how connections and pivots are established from photos and recorded, and the real tree of Rig B as built, with its 20 joints and 14 reference frames. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Filling gaps (augmentation)](40-method/filling-gaps.md): How values that the photos do not give are filled in, how each value says where it came from, what the build enforces so invented values cannot pass as measured, and how a real measurement overrides an estimate. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Measuring from photos](40-method/measuring-from-photos.md): The measuring procedure as executed for Rig B - camera from metadata, structure from motion, bundle adjustment in a model frame fixed on the platform deck, scale closure against purchased parts, triangulation and single-view rays, honest classes and ranges, and what the photos cannot check. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The pipeline, end to end](40-method/pipeline.md): How eleven phone photos became a parametric, articulated 3D asset and a browser viewer; each stage with its inputs, outputs, command, who does it and how long it took on this machine. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*

## Implementation

- [Deployment](50-implementation/deployment.md): Every push to main deploys automatically; bun run deploy does the same by hand. It checks everything, builds the viewer, model, wiki and (since platform step 1) the server into one release, uploads it through a restricted account, switches the site atomically, checks it over HTTPS and switches back on failure. The server's own service and its one-time host setup (done on 2026-11-24) are on a page of their own. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
- [Measurement results](50-implementation/measurement-results.md): What the photos gave for Rig B - the scale closes within 0-2 % against purchased parts, five cameras were solved, 118 dimensions were recorded with a class and a range, and all three of the owner's figures conflict with the photos. Nothing here has been checked against a tape measure. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Modelling rounds](50-implementation/modeling-rounds.md): The model's story in pictures - two planning trials that silently lacked the left pod, a complete blockout, a first formed model that the independent reviewer rejected as "in between" (8 of 45 components rejected), a second round that closed 24 of 28 findings and was accepted after three small fixes, and a third round of those fixes. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The rigtwin server and its host setup](50-implementation/server-and-host-setup.md): Platform step 1's server on the production host - one hardened Bun service on 127.0.0.1:4190 behind one Caddy route, installed once by a reviewed setup script with fourteen host checks. The setup ran on 2026-11-24 with the owner's yes, and the server has been live since the release of that evening. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
- [Tech stack as built](50-implementation/tech-stack.md): Bun and TypeScript, with three.js the only library that reaches the browser; Python reads the model file independently; headless Chromium makes every render. Since platform step 1 a small Bun server with no added package holds the shared scene (commands over HTTP, changes as server-sent events). Six pinned npm packages, all MIT or Apache-2.0; no Blender or photogrammetry. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
- [Timeline and performance](50-implementation/timeline-and-performance.md): How long everything took on 2026-11-23, phase by phase - about 3.5 hours of planning with 16 agents, then 2 hours 46 minutes from the first implementation step to the round-2 verdict with 14 agent runs - with every agent run's duration, tokens and tool calls, the measured run times of every tool, and the model's size at each stage. All figures come from one Apple M2 machine and one run. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [The viewer](50-implementation/viewer.md): The browser viewer shows the rig, lets a person turn, zoom, hide and adjust its parts, and makes every render. Rebuilt after two interface reviews from 103 controls to 16, with 83 % of the window for the model and 53 acceptance checks passing. Since platform step 1 it is a live client of the shared scene: changes are saved for everyone, others' appear with who did what and an Undo. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*

## Results

- [Critique](70-results/critique.md): An honest list of what is weak in the result - the model (sizes never taped, depth seen from one viewpoint, borrowed left side, assumed adjustments and pivots), the method (no planted-error test of the reviewer, no human gates, one object and one run, builders and reviewers of one model family, scale resting on one spoken figure), the viewer, the documentation and the process. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Gallery](70-results/gallery.md): Every picture of the project in order - the eleven masked source photos by rig, the planning trials, the blockout, modelling rounds 1 to 3 with the reviewers' sheets, the final model from several views, the model laid over the photos, and the browser viewer before and after its redesign - each with a caption saying what to look at. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Goal assessment](70-results/goal-assessment.md): Of 69 requirements, 55 are met, 11 partly, none not met and 3 not yet done (GitHub and the production wiki). The run shows a credible, modular, parametric, articulated model built from casual photos by AI agents, with honest provenance; it does not show that the sizes are right or that the Skill transfers to another object. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Model card of the Rig B asset](70-results/rig-b-model-card.md): What the Rig B asset is, what it is for and what it must not be used for - 46 parts in five groups, 20 joints (6 of them assumed), 14 reference frames and 305 parameter records with their sources and ranges, built from eleven photos; sizes are photo estimates never checked against a tape, and all three of the owner's figures conflict with the photos. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*

- [Agent interface](80-reference/agent-interface.md): How an agent drives the shared scene - five MCP tools (adjust, look, measure, undo, state) served by the rigtwin server itself, the same locally and on mightwork.ai, with every adjustment's meaning in one generated catalogue. This page is generated from the code (bun tools/agent-docs.ts); bun run check fails when it is out of date. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
- [Skills and agents](80-reference/skills-and-agents.md): The Agent Skill "modeling-3d-assets-from-references" (version 0.1.0) and three agent definitions that package the modelling method for the next asset, and the operating Skill "operating-rigtwin" (v0) that tells Claude Code how to change, show, measure and undo things in the shared scene; what each holds, how to invoke it, what is unexercised and how the Skills are refined. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
- [Research sources](80-reference/sources.md): One short section for each of the sixteen documents behind the plan (eight specialist reports, two critiques, five adversarial reviews, one closure check), giving the question it answered, what it established with the key numbers, what it could not verify, and which wiki pages carry its content. The full texts are in the project's private archive. *(stable, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Human-factors standards and the seat reference](80-reference/standards.md): Which ergonomic standards bear on a seated remote-operation station, as far as this project established it, what each would need from the 3D asset, and why the asset carries "estimated seat reference" frames instead of a standardised seat index point. No standard was read in full; every statement is marked read in part or recalled, and must be confirmed against purchased texts. *(living, updated 2026-11-23)*
- [Tool reference](80-reference/tools.md): Every command of the project (build, check, render, serve, rig, dist, wiki, deploy; the acceptance, live and deploy tests; the setup script; the independent model reader) with its options, outputs and typical run time, plus the shared scene's commands, the viewer's URL and script interface, the workspaces and where every output goes. *(living, updated 2026-11-24)*
